name: military-space-rockets-and-fusion
description: Military Science, Rockets, Space, Fusion, and Mars: strategic theory and engineering physics in one reference, at the war-college survey level for the first and the engineering level for the rest. Military science as the one field whose object of study is a reactive adversary, so no principle holds unconditionally — war as a political instrument or nothing, defence as an economic and industrial problem first, institutional learning as the hardest capability to copy; Clausewitz's trinity, friction, centre of gravity, culminating point and defence as the stronger form, Sun Tzu and Jomini and Soviet operational art, Mahan against Corbett, and the air power promise against the post-1945 bombing surveys; the three levels of war and why tactical success does not aggregate into strategic success, the principles as contradictory heuristics, manoeuvre versus attrition, OODA with ORIENT restored, mission command; deterrence by punishment and by denial, Schelling on compellence, the stability-instability paradox and the measurement problem, survivability and the triad, Kahn's escalation thresholds and off-ramps, alliance abandonment versus entrapment, and grand strategy as ends, ways and means — with the near-miss record and the line that deterrence working for decades is compatible with having been repeatedly lucky. Then the readiness/modernization/size trilemma, logistics and the industrial base as the professional's subject, doctrine and its rigidity paradox, intelligence failing analytically rather than collectively, procurement's monopsony structure, modern conflict from the counter-UAS cost-per-engagement problem through cyber, Kessler syndrome and information operations to total defence — and the law of armed conflict in full: jus ad bellum against jus in bello, the equality of application, distinction, proportionality stated correctly rather than as a casualty comparison, military necessity, humanity, and command responsibility. Rocket engineering from Tsiolkovsky and the 94%-propellant example, the structural coefficient and why SSTO is marginal, v_e proportional to the square root of T_c/M_w and why engines run fuel-rich, the c*/C_F factorization, flow separation and the Summerfield criterion, L* and injector families, the engine-cycle table and the expander cycle's geometric ceiling, throat heat flux and the Bartz correlation, and propellants chosen on density impulse rather than Isp alone. Vis-viva and why orbital energy depends only on the semi-major axis, the Hohmann worked example, plane change and launch-site latitude as a hard constraint, the Oberth effect, J₂ exploited by sun-synchronous and Molniya orbits, the ascent Δv budget with gravity loss dominant, max-Q and q·α, buckling knockdown factors and balloon tanks, POGO, lossless convexification, reentry heating as compression rather than friction with Sutton-Graves and the ±1° Apollo corridor, and normalization of deviance at Challenger and Columbia. Spacecraft design under mass, distance and human physiology, with the design cascade, the 1/r² partition of the solar system, RTGs, the T⁴ radiator numbers, link budgets and light-time, fault protection as its own hazard, wheel saturation, the Mars EDL squeeze and its one-tonne ceiling, the career radiation dose a Mars mission exceeds, ECLSS closure and the 93%-to-98% gap, MOXIE, and the margin schedule with the failures that produced it. Fusion as energy, not weapons: the binding energy curve, the Coulomb barrier and the 10–15 keV requirement, why D-T wins despite putting 80% of its energy in a neutron, the Lawson triple product attacked from opposite directions by magnetic and inertial confinement, tokamaks against stellarators, disruptions and divertor load, Rayleigh-Taylor and repetition rate, tritium breeding, 14 MeV neutron damage with no qualified material, HTS magnets and B⁴ scaling — and Q_scientific against Q_engineering, with NIF's reported gain measured against laser energy delivered to the target rather than wall-plug draw. Satellites by orbit regime, flight software where you cannot patch your way out and the hardware flips its own bits, FDIR with isolation as the hardest step, CCSDS, Voyager patched 46 years after launch, and planetary protection closing off exactly the regions where the astrobiology is. And Mars end to end: 610 Pa and why liquid water cannot exist stably, 3.71 m/s² and the unknown of whether 0.38 g protects, solar-wind stripping, dust storms cutting irradiance by up to 97%, the mine-to-methalox ISRU chain and the 1–2 MWe that puts fission power in the critical path, the 26-month window and the 1–1.5 tonne parachute ceiling, food as the largest unclosed loop, then terraforming with the Armstrong limit and three distinct habitability thresholds, manufactured super-greenhouse gases as the only physically plausible gas source, warming given as both 100–500 years and 1,000–10,000 years, the magnetic field problem and the oxygen problem both left unsolved, paraterraforming, the ethics of deliberate contamination, and why Venus is harder still. Strategic theory and engineering physics only: no weapon design, yield, device physics, targeting or employment detail, because the source contains none.
